stories.headline: Houthis Seize Yemeni Lands as Tanker Attack Hits Strait of Hormuz
stories.body:
Houthi rebel forces seized the Yemeni port of Mokha [c13]. The forces also took Mayyun Island near the Bab el-Mandab strait [c13]. The Saudi-backed Yemeni government lost these key coastal oil shipping lands to the Iran-aligned Houthis [c7]. Fighting across Yemen has displaced about 100,000 people [c9].

A projectile hit the MT El Gaia tanker over the weekend in the Strait of Hormuz [c1]. The ship was sailing in dark mode with its identification system turned off [c1]. The tanker carried 25 crew members [c2]. Among them were 14 Indian nationals [c2]. The ship also carried 11 Pakistani nationals [c2].

Pakistani Third Engineer Muhammad Hammad Obaida is missing after an engine room watch [c3]. Indian Oiler Sumit Kumar Singh is also missing [c3]. The Omani Coast Guard brought 23 remaining crew members ashore [c4].

Iran's IRGC Navy said the ship hit naval mines on an illegal route [c5]. But the US said a missile and a drone hit the vessel [c5].

Only four ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday [c12]. Before the war, about 130 ships crossed each day [c12]. Saudi Aramco closed its East-West pipeline after a Houthi attack [c11]. Oil loadings stopped at the Saudi port of Yanbu [c10]. The price of Brent crude rose nearly 3% to $108 a barrel [c10].

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman talked with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo [c6]. They called for free navigation in the Red Sea [c6]. Egypt lost about $7 billion from the Suez Canal between 2023 and 2024 [c8]. This was about 60 percent of canal revenues [c8].

vocab.meaning: an object fired or thrown as a weapon
forced to leave home or country

stories.headline: NATO Intercepts Drone Over Lithuania as Baltic Tensions Rise
stories.body:
NATO fighter jets shot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace overnight [c16]. The interception took place near the village of Pratkūnai [c16]. An Italian fighter jet carried out the shootdown for NATO [c19]. The unmanned aircraft had entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus [c19].

Lithuanian Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas commented on the downed drone [c17]. Kaunas said authorities detected an explosive device on the drone [c17]. Bomb-disposal experts were called to the site [c17]. The experts neutralized the explosive device [c17].

Military actions also escalated elsewhere in the region [c20]. Poland scrambled its own fighter jets as a preventive step [c20]. Russian jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles were carrying out strikes on Ukrainian territory [c20].

Polish security forces later found a drone in the Baltic Sea [c21]. The aircraft was identified as a Russian drone [c21]. Forces recovered it near the beach in the town of Rusinowo [c21].

Denmark reported another dangerous event in the Baltic Sea [c18]. A Russian frigate fired flares at a Danish air force helicopter [c18]. The helicopter was performing routine surveillance work [c18]. The incident occurred off Gedser in the Baltic Sea [c18].

Danish Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus released details of the confrontation [c22]. Bruus said the Russian ship fired two flares at the helicopter [c22]. The warship gave no prior warning before firing [c22]. One of the flares passed within metres of the aircraft [c22].

Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador to respond to the flare incident [c23]. The summons concerned the threat to the Danish air force helicopter [c23].

Russian ambassador Vladimir Barbin addressed the Danish accusations [c24]. Barbin said Russia would thoroughly investigate the incident [c24]. But Barbin accused Danish helicopters of taking provocative actions [c24]. He said these actions occurred near Russian warships [c24].

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made a statement on retaliatory strikes [c25]. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces struck an oil refinery located in Syzran, Russia [c25]. He said the strike was a direct response to Russian attacks [c25]. Russia had targeted Ukraine's energy infrastructure [c25].

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov commented on energy infrastructure attacks [c26]. Peskov mentioned a proposal from Donald Trump [c26]. Trump proposed a ceasefire on energy infrastructure [c26]. Peskov said the Kremlin considers Trump's proposal a good idea [c26].

vocab.meaning: careful watching of an area or activity
intended to cause anger or action

stories.headline: US War With Iran Costs Billions and Depletes Interceptor Stockpiles
stories.body:
The Congressional Budget Office reported that the war with Iran has cost the US military $38 billion [c27]. This figure covers costs up to August 1, 2026 [c27]. The report estimated the conflict adds $3 billion in military costs for every extra month [c28]. Rebuilding the depleted US stockpile of interceptors will take at least five years [c29]. These include Patriot, Thaad, and Navy interceptors [c29].

A Pentagon inspector general report showed the US spent $22.3 billion on munitions alone through June 30 [c30]. Total spending on the conflict reached $33.4 billion by that date [c30]. The CBO estimated the US has used between one-half and two-thirds of its missile defense interceptors since June 2025 [c31]. CSIS estimated Patriot interceptors dropped from about 2,330 before the war to between 759 and 827 by July 27 [c37].

President Donald Trump denied reports of weapons shortages [c32]. Trump claimed US munitions supplies are virtually unlimited [c32].

The US military lost four F-15E fighter jets, one F-35 fighter, and 30 MQ-9 Reaper drones through June 30 [c33]. Three F-15E jets were destroyed by friendly fire over Kuwait on March 1 [c35]. Another was lost over Iran in April [c35]. At least 11 US service members died in action through June 30 [c36]. Seven died in non-hostile events [c36]. Another 417 were wounded [c36].

The White House requested $87.6 billion in extra funding in June [c34]. The request set aside $67.1 billion for the Department of Defense [c34].

vocab.meaning: a missile designed to destroy incoming enemy weapons

stories.headline: Supreme Court Blocks Mail-In Ballot Restrictions Ahead of Midterm Elections
stories.body:
The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's plan for new Postal Service rules on mail-in ballots [c40]. The decision comes ahead of the November 3 midterm elections [c40]. Justice Brett Kavanaugh agreed with the decision [c41]. Kavanaugh said state and local officials lacked enough time to implement the rule before the election [c41]. Supreme Court Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented from the ruling [c43].

President Donald Trump criticized Justices Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett on Truth Social [c42]. Trump said they are not the people he interviewed [c42].

Attorney General Todd Blanche said that the court decision will not affect ongoing criminal investigations into illegal voting [c38]. In Texas, federal prosecutors charged six lawful permanent residents and one undocumented immigrant for voting in federal elections over eight years [c39].

US District Judge Deborah Boardman issued an injunction on September 2 [c44]. The ruling blocked Donald Trump's executive order targeting birth tourism [c44].

Mail-in voting for the midterm elections has already begun in several states [c45]. These states include Alabama, North Carolina, and Wisconsin [c45].

stories.headline: United States Confirms Deployment of Weapons in Earth Orbit
stories.body:
The United States confirmed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space [c46]. US Air Force Secretary Troy Meink spoke about the weapons at a conference [c48]. Meink said the US has on-orbit space control weapons [c48]. He said these weapons can defend forces against hostile actions [c48].

Victoria Samson of the Secure World Foundation commented on the systems [c49]. Samson suggested the newly acknowledged weapons could be space-based jammers [c49].

Russia and China warned of an arms race in outer space after the announcement [c47]. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun urged the US to stop expanding military capabilities in space [c51]. Guo also asked the US to stop preparing for war in outer space [c51]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia counts on international efforts to completely demilitarise space [c52].

Dr. Bleddyn Bowen said China has shown space tug capability [c53]. This allows a vehicle to grab a satellite and move it into another orbit [c53]. India conducted an Anti-Satellite missile test in March 2019 under Mission Shakti [c50]. That test destroyed an Indian satellite in low-Earth orbit [c50].

vocab.meaning: to remove military weapons or forces from an area
the path of an object around a planet or star

stories.headline: India Introduces Merchant Fees for UPI Payments Over 2,000 Rupees
stories.body:
The National Payments Corporation of India introduced a new fee framework for UPI merchant payments [c54]. The Merchant Discount Rate framework takes effect on October 15 [c54]. NPCI issued a circular about the rule on Tuesday, September 15, 2026 [c62].

Under the framework, customers will pay no charges for making UPI payments [c55]. This zero-fee rule for consumers applies regardless of transaction value [c55]. NPCI explicitly barred UPI app providers from charging platform fees to consumers [c73]. App providers are also barred from adding any other charges to consumers for UPI payments [c73].

Merchants receiving UPI payments above Rs 2,000 in a single transaction will pay a 0.4% fee [c56]. The fee is capped at a maximum of Rs 300 [c56]. Small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month will pay no fees on incoming payments [c59].

The Union Ministry of Finance issued the official notification under Section 10A of the 2007 Payment and Settlement Systems Act [c70]. Parliament passed the 2026 Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill in August 2026 [c71]. That bill amended the 2007 law to allow charges on UPI and RuPay debit card payments [c71].

The Indian government said that data analysis shows only 4% of merchant UPI transactions will be impacted [c64]. Standard credit card fees typically range from 1.5% to 2.5% per transaction, according to NPCI [c72].

The Finance Ministry said that collected fees will be shared among payment participants [c57]. These participants include banks and app providers [c57]. The money will support operations and system expansion [c57]. A dedicated fund will receive 5% of total MDR collections [c65]. This fund will promote UPI usage by small merchants [c65].

A flat fee of Rs 5 will apply to UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 in essential sectors [c60]. These sectors include railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel, and agricultural inputs [c60]. Essential sectors account for nearly 17% of merchant UPI transaction volume [c69]. They also account for around 46% of merchant transaction value [c69].

Capital market transactions will attract a fee of 0.02% [c61]. This applies to mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers, and dealers [c61]. The fee is capped at Rs 300 per transaction [c61].

Person-to-person UPI transfers will remain completely free for individuals [c58]. These transfers account for 37% of total UPI transaction volume [c63]. They also account for 70% of total UPI transaction value [c58][c63].

Opposition parties in India criticized the new fee [c66]. They called the charge the "Modi tax" [c66]. Congress media head Pawan Khera spoke out against Prime Minister Narendra Modi [c67]. Khera said Modi popularised UPI for a cashless economy and is now taxing people for using it [c67]. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged that Modi surrendered to American pressure [c68]. Gandhi said American payment companies had opposed India's zero-fee policy [c68].

vocab.meaning: a basic structure of rules or ideas
a complex network of connected parts
